docs.title: BuildService
docs.text:
Welcome to BuildService - The first public and open-source plot-based freecam sandbox building system.

Special note: This project is completely open-source, meaning that anyone can use the system without permissions or limitations. That being said, lot of time, thought, and effort has gone into this project, and supporting this project is always appreciated and acknowledged on our supporters page. Thank you!

View documentation | View installation instructions | Support us!

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The BuildService project serves to provide a prebuilt, customizable, advanced, and open-source "build mode" for developers. It's goal is to minimize the time and effort developers put in to making a production game while still providing as many features as possible.

As far as BuildService features, here is a list of notable features BuildService offers: * Plot selection system * Save selection system * Plot serialization and saving (Support for external DataStore solutions) * Save loading system (Support for external DataStore solutions) * Assignable values to objects, walls, paint, materials, etc. (Support for external economy system) * Plot freecam * Grid snap placement * Smooth snapping (Interpolation between snapped positions) * Placement in plot bounds * Object placement * Wall placement * Floor placement * Roof placement * Window/door placement * Room detection * Multiple "levels" (Basements, upper floors, etc.) * Transform tool (Scale, move along axis, etc.) * Paint tool (Customizable coloring options for objects) * Server validated placement

There are several additional features not listed that make BuildService even more amazing. All features are highlighted in the documentation page

docs.title: API
docs.text: Welcome to the BuildService API. This page serves to provide every detail about BuildService, including it's functions, properties, values, and how BuildService works. Thank you for choosing BuildService

docs.title: BuildService Client
docs.text: All of the client module properties and methods

docs.title: .Collision
docs.text:
BuildService.Collision   [RBXScriptSignal]

A signal that is fired every time a placement is attempted, but the placing object collides with an object that was already placed. This makes it easy to implement UI-based warnings to the player about collisions.

Example usage:

local lastCollision = 0

BuildService.Collision:Connect(function()
    warningLabel.Visible = true
    lastCollision = tick()

    task.wait(3)

    if tick() - lastCollision >= 3 then
        warningLabel.Visible = false
    end
end)

Warning

It's important to note that this event is fired every time a client attempts to place an object and there is a collision error. Repeated placement could result in several connections happening very frequently. If not handled properly, timed UI-based warnings could break.

docs.title: .Error
docs.text:
BuildService.Error   [RBXScriptSignal]

A signal that is fired every time an error is raised from BuildService on the client.

Example usage:

BuildService.Error:Connect(function(warning: string)
    error("[BuildService] - " .. warning)
end)

Note

Typically, BuildService errors should not happen. The only reason these errors might occur is because of definition errors in the configuration module. If you are getting errors from BuildService, please check that the configuration paths are correct.

docs.title: .SessionActive
docs.text:
BuildService.SessionActive   [bool] (read-only)

A read-only value that external scripts can read to view the session status. If the value is true, a session is currently active. If the value is false, a session is not currently active.

docs.title: .SessionChanged
docs.text:
BuildService.SessionChanged   [RBXScriptSignal]

A signal that is fired every time the BuildService.SessionActive value is changed.

Example usage:

BuildService.SessionChanged:Connect(function(active: boolean)
    sessionStatusValue.Text = active and "Active" or "Inactive"
end)

docs.title: .Warning
docs.text:
BuildService.Warning   [RBXScriptSignal]

A signal that is fired every time a warning is raised from BuildService on the client.

Example usage:

BuildService.Warning:Connect(function(warning: string)
    warn("[BuildService] - " .. warning)
end)

Note

BuildService warnings are not fatal. Script execution should not halt due to warnings. The system handles the events that cause the warnings to occur automatically.

docs.title: :RequestSessionStart()
docs.text:
BuildService:RequestSessionStart()

Sends a request to the server through the BuildRequest RemoteFunction.

If the BuildRequest RemoteFunction returns true, the function will update BuildService.SessionActive to true and start the freecam if it's enabled in the BuildConfig Module.

If there is a problem starting a session, the BuildService.Warning event will be fired with the problem details.

Example usage:

startButton.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
    BuildService:RequestSessionStart()
end)

docs.title: :RequestSessionStop()
docs.text:
BuildService:RequestSessionStop()

Sends a request to the server through the BuildRequest RemoteFunction.

If the BuildRequest RemoteFunction returns true, the function will update BuildService.SessionActive to false and stop the freecam.

If there is a problem stopping the session, the BuildService.Warning event will be fired with the problem details.

Example usage:

stopButton.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
    BuildService:RequestSessionStop()
end)

docs.title: :SelectObject()
docs.text:
BuildService:SelectObject(objectName: string)

Attempts to start object placement given the objectName parameter. The function will attempt to find the object model from the objectName parameter in the objectsFolder defined in the BuildConfig Module.

Any problems that occur while selecting an object, such as an object not being found, will fire the BuildService.Warning event with the problem details.

Example usage:

objectButton.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
    BuildService:SelectObject(objectButton.Name)
end)

Note

In the above example, the system is set up to select objects based on the clicked button's name.

docs.title: :SelectWall()
docs.text:
BuildService:SelectWall()

Attempts to start wall placement, using the configuration for wall placement defined in the BuildConfig Module.

Any problems that occur while placing walls will fire the BuildService.Warning event with the problem details.

Example usage:

wallButton.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
    BuildService:SelectWall()
end)

docs.title: BuildConfig Module
docs.text: A module containing all of the defualt configurations for BuildService. This module is read-only, meaning that external scripts can only read information from it, but cannot write new information to it.

docs.title: GRID_SIZES
docs.text:
Config.GRID_SIZES   [table] -- {number}

A table of numbers representing grid sizes, in studs, that can be cycled through.

Note

To disable the grid, set the only size to be 0.

Config.GRID_SIZES = {0}

docs.title: GRID_TEXTURE_ID
docs.text:
Config.GRID_TEXTURE_ID   [number] -- Image ID

The image ID of the grid texture to be displayed on the plot during placement sessions.

Note

Set the ID to 0 to disable the grid texture.

docs.title: ALLOW_GRID_TOGGLE
docs.text:
Config.ALLOW_GRID_TOGGLE   [bool]

Allow players to toggle the grid. If enabled, players can toggle between placing objects freely in the plot or snapping objects to a grid.

docs.title: GRID_TOGGLE_GAMEPASS
docs.text:
Config.GRID_TOGGLE_GAMEPASS   [number] -- Gamepass ID

If players are able to toggle the grid on and off, this is an optional gamepass that players would be required to own before toggling the grid.

Note

Set the ID to 0 to disable the gamepass requirement
